abstract: Laminins are large, heterotrimeric glycoproteins that are a major structural component of basement membranes and the extracellular matrix. Although they are difficult to produce recombinantly because of their large size, a smaller fragment of the laminin heterotrimer that supports cell adhesion and cell migration, termed E8, can be recombinantly expressed. Here, we use AlphaFold to optimize laminin E8 fragments and design a panel of interchangeable laminin , {beta}, and {gamma} chains that can be combined to produce all isoforms recombinantly. These recombinant E8 fragments support adhesion of cells bearing their cognate integrins, and will be useful tools for stem-cell, organoid, and laminin-binding integrin biology research.
